_comment: Tier-2 for kratos.mpm pitfall #7: solver_settings.solver_type takes a short label, not a solver class name. FALSE CLAIM CORRECTED. The catalog served MPMStaticSolver / MPMQuasiStaticSolver / MPMImplicitDynamicSolver / MPMExplicitSolver as the MPM 'solver_types', which reads as the value to write into ProjectParameters. Executed 2026-08-07 on Kratos 10.4.3 Release with MPMApplication, calling python_solvers_wrapper_mpm.CreateSolver directly so no mesh is needed: all four class-name spellings are rejected with Exception 'The requested solver type "<x>" is not in the python solvers wrapper' + 'Available options are: "static", "dynamic", "quasi_static"', while static, quasi_static and dynamic all get past the label check. The wrapper also accepts the capitalised variants Static, Quasi-static and Dynamic, and for dynamic it then requires a second key time_integration_method with value implicit or explicit. Note the fixture counts 'accepted' as anything that gets PAST the label check -- a later failure on a missing mdpa or a missing key still counts as accepted, because the claim under test is about the label, not about a complete deck. INTERPRETER: needs a Kratos build carrying MPMApplication; set KRATOS_PYTHON. MUTATION CONTROL (T2_MUTATE=1, re-runnable): the mutation INVERTS the accept/reject expectation for all seven spellings -- asserting the four class names are accepted and the three real labels are not -- while leaving the CreateSolver call untouched, so it proves each verdict comes from a real wrapper invocation rather than an echoed table. Verified: unmutated PASSES (rc=0) with solver_type_mismatches=0; with T2_MUTATE=1 it FAILS (rc=1) and solver_type_mismatches goes to 7, with every accepted[...]_expected=... line disagreeing with itself. Re-verify: cd scripts/tier2_fixtures/kratos/mpm_solver_type_is_a_label_not_a_class && $KRATOS_PYTHON source.py (passes), then T2_MUTATE=1 $KRATOS_PYTHON source.py (fails). FIXED 2026-08-08 (forbid changed): forbid_in_output was 'MISMATCH', matched by the runner as a plain case-insensitive substring -- and this fixture's own SUCCESS line is '{key}=0', which contains 'mismatch'. The tripwire therefore fired on the line that says nothing went wrong, so the fixture was red on every run whatever Kratos did, and the red carried no information. The needle is now 'MISMATCH: ' with the colon, which only the per-case failure print emits. PROVEN BY EXECUTION 2026-08-08 on Kratos 10.4.3 with KRATOS_PYTHON=/mnt/kratos-tier2/kv/bin/python, through scripts/run_tier2_fixtures.py --fixture: unmutated PASSES; T2_MUTATE=1 emits 'MISMATCH: ' lines and a non-zero count, rc=1. Before the change the runner reported "forbidden tokens appeared: ['MISMATCH']" on the unmutated run.
